title: Area of the boundary of the Mandelbrot set
premise_risks: Famous and probably very hard (low novelty). It is listed because it is important and has a one-line Lean statement.
It should be checked against the scorer's view of whether it duplicates the existing hyperbolic-measure item QED-M051. It does not: that item asks about the computability of a real-line measure.
plain: The Mandelbrot set M is the set of complex numbers c for which the orbit of 0 under z -> z^2 + c stays bounded. Its boundary is a fractal of Hausdorff dimension 2, as large as possible for a plane set. Does the boundary of M have zero area?
math: Let $M=\{c\in\mathbb C:\sup_n|f_c^{n}(0)|<\infty\}$ with $f_c(z)=z^2+c$. Decide whether the two-dimensional Lebesgue measure of $\partial M$ is $0$.
